evidence: Harness note: "this run had no domain owner to ask. The bootstrap prompt inlined the scenario and told the agent that no interactive partner was present" — the agent was given nobody to interrogate.
"Assistant turns before the agent first wrote a file: 19" — the agent did not jump straight to scaffolding; it spent nineteen turns before the first Write.

Absent: no record of any question posed to a domain owner, and no record of an ontology sketch being stated for confirmation before the first Write. The corpus itself carries no trace of a dialogue (no captured exchange, no open questions attributed to an owner).

The one substitute for dialogue that is visible in the artifact is the class schema being fixed before instances: seven `.ont.yml` class definitions with declared `edges:` blocks (e.g. `identification.ont.yml` declares `requires → assumption`, `targets → estimand`, `threatened-by ← confounding`, `enabled-by ← study-design`) that every later instance node conforms to.
criteria.rationale: The criterion is unscorable as written — the harness supplied no interlocutor, so a count of zero questions is an artifact of the setup rather than a fact about the agent. What the run does show is 19 turns of deliberation and a schema settled before instances were written, which is evidence of restraint but not of interrogation.

evidence: `exclusion-restriction.yml`: "the instrument Z affects the outcome Y only through its effect on the treatment D" — one assumption, one node; the IV *estimator* and the IV *identification strategy* live in separate files (`two-stage-least-squares.yml`, `instrumental-variable-identification.yml`).

The estimand / identification / estimator triad is split three ways rather than fused: `average-treatment-effect.yml` (the target), `backdoor-identification.yml` (whether it is recoverable), `inverse-probability-weighting.yml` (the procedure). `estimand/README.md` states the separation explicitly: "a study that identifies the LATE but estimates the ATE has not estimated what it identified."

`sutva.yml` covers two sub-clauses — "(1) no interference … and (2) no hidden treatment versions" — but these are the two halves of one conventionally-named assumption, not two concepts filed together.

`inverse-probability-weighting.yml` closes with an AIPW passage — "Augmented IPW (AIPW) addresses the propensity misspecification problem…" — tagged `[inference]` and framed as an extension of the node's subject rather than a second co-equal concept.
criteria.rationale: Each of the thirteen instance nodes carries exactly one concept, and the corpus holds the three most easily-fused ideas in the field — estimand, identification, estimator — apart by construction. The only multi-part node (SUTVA) is a single named assumption with two clauses.

evidence: `conditional-ignorability.yml`: "(Y(0), Y(1)) ⊥⊥ T | X", with `testability: "Partially: balance checks assess covariate balance post-adjustment but cannot verify balance on unmeasured variables. Sensitivity analysis (Rosenbaum bounds, E-value) quantifies robustness to violations."`

`two-stage-least-squares.yml`: "The first-stage F-statistic is a standard diagnostic for instrument strength; F < 10 is a conventional warning threshold, though more modern tests (effective F-statistic) are preferred."

`instrumental-variable-identification.yml`: "LATE = Cov(Y,Z)/Cov(D,Z)", plus `identification_status: "LATE is identified when all three IV conditions hold; ATE is not identified by IV alone without homogeneity assumptions"`.

`backdoor-identification.yml`: "A set X satisfies the backdoor criterion relative to (T, Y) if: (i) no node in X is a descendant of T, and (ii) X blocks every path between T and Y that contains an arrow into T", with the identifying functional "∑_x P(Y | T=t, X=x)P(X=x)".

`exclusion-restriction.yml` `violation_consequence`: "IV estimator converges to a weighted average of the LATE and the direct instrument effect, not the LATE — the bias direction depends on the sign of the direct effect."
criteria.rationale: Nodes state formal conditions, named diagnostics with thresholds, and specific failure modes — content that is specific enough to be checked and specific enough to be wrong. No node restates its own label.

evidence: `inverse-probability-weighting.yml` links: `recovers → estimand/average-treatment-effect`, `valid-under → assumption/conditional-ignorability`, `operationalizes → identification/backdoor-identification` — three different relationship kinds to three different classes of thing, each naming a mechanism.

`unmeasured-confounder.yml`: `threatens → identification/backdoor-identification` and `violates-when-present → assumption/conditional-ignorability`, backed in the node body by the mechanism "U → T and U → Y, creating a backdoor path T ← U → Y that is not blocked by the observed adjustment set X."

`natural-experiment.yml`: `supports → assumption/exclusion-restriction`, `enables → identification/instrumental-variable-identification` — the design-to-assumption link that `study-design/README.md` names as the point of the class: "the study design is the empirical basis for the assumption."

Every instance also carries a structural `instance-of → ../<class>.ont.yml` edge, but in no node is it the only link; the thinnest instance node (`binary-treatment-intervention.yml`) still carries two `defines` edges to ATE and LATE.

Three edges assert more than the field supports: `average-treatment-effect.yml` → `decomposes-into → local-average-treatment-effect` (the LATE is the effect on a subpopulation, not a decomposition of the ATE); `natural-experiment.yml` → `rules-out → confounding/selection-bias`; and `selection-bias.yml` → `does-not-threaten → identification/instrumental-variable-identification` (sample-selection into the study threatens IV as much as any design).
criteria.rationale: The edge vocabulary is relational rather than filing — `requires`, `operationalizes`, `recovers`, `threatens`, `valid-under`, `enables` — and the mechanisms behind the edges are stated in the node bodies. A handful of edges overclaim, but they are wrong-content edges, not directory citations.

evidence: Subject names the domain: "genesis: causal inference in observational studies — 7 classes, 13 instances, 2 calculator stubs", and the body restates the central question: "Domain: how do we identify causal effects from data not generated by a randomized experiment?"

The ontology is described class by class with a gloss on each, not merely listed: "confounding (disposition) — variables that induce non-causal treatment-outcome associations", "identification (quality) — conditions under which a causal estimand is recoverable", "assumption (quality) — unverifiable conditions required for identification to hold".

A dedicated "Key relationships established" section names seven edges, e.g. "backdoor-identification requires conditional-ignorability and sutva, targets ATE" and "natural-experiment enables IV identification, rules out selection-bias, supports exclusion-restriction".
No line of the message is a bare filename list; the seed-instance roster is grouped by class rather than by path.
criteria.rationale: The message names the domain, glosses every class in the schema, and devotes a section to the relationships rather than to the files — a reader who saw only this commit would know what the ontology asserts.

evidence: All thirteen instances are kinds, not specimens: `conditional-ignorability`, `sutva`, `exclusion-restriction`, `unmeasured-confounder`, `selection-bias`, `average-treatment-effect`, `local-average-treatment-effect`, `binary-treatment-intervention`, `natural-experiment`, `backdoor-identification`, `instrumental-variable-identification`, `inverse-probability-weighting`, `two-stage-least-squares`.

Absent: no node is a named study, dataset, paper, or dated analysis. `natural-experiment.yml` is the nearest risk and stays at the class level — concrete cases appear inside the prose as illustrations, not as nodes: "Classic examples include lottery-based draft assignment for military service, geographic or date-of-birth discontinuities in program eligibility."

The two-tier split is schema, not drift: `.ont.yml` files define the class (`estimand.ont.yml`: `properties:` / `edges:`) and the sibling directory holds instances of it, and every instance declares `instance-of → ../<class>.ont.yml`.
Within each class the members sit at one grain — the estimand class holds ATE and LATE (both population-level contrasts); the estimator class holds IPW and 2SLS (both procedures).
criteria.rationale: The corpus holds one level — general kinds within a declared class schema — throughout, with concrete cases confined to illustrative prose. There is no mixing of classes with named specimens.

evidence: Reference: "something about the nature of causation vs. correlation" — `intervention.ont.yml`: "The act of externally setting a variable's value — Pearl's do-operator — which is conceptually and mathematically distinct from passively observing that variable take a value", and `intervention/README.md` sharpens it: "what separates asking 'what is the probability that Y = 1 given X = 1?' from asking 'what would be the probability that Y = 1 if we *set* X = 1?'"

Reference: "the role of assumptions" — a whole class, framed exactly as the reference does: `assumption.ont.yml`: "assumptions are the price of identification in observational studies", with three seeds (ignorability, SUTVA, exclusion restriction).

Reference: "what identification requires" — `identification/README.md`: "An estimand is *identified* when it can be expressed as a functional of the observable data distribution… If an estimand is not identified, no statistical estimator can recover it, regardless of sample size", plus two strategies with their graph conditions.

Reference: "reflect the tension between the formal and the applied" — carried in the `testability` property across assumption nodes and in `[open]` tags: "In many natural experiment designs, violations of the exclusion restriction are the most contested identification threat"; "Whether the complier population is policy-relevant in any given application is a substantive question the data cannot answer."
Deviation in scale: the reference asks for "3–4 well-linked corpus nodes"; the run produced 7 class definitions and 13 instances, roughly four times the described seed.
criteria.rationale: All three required content areas are present as first-class structure, and the formal/applied tension is carried in a dedicated property rather than gestured at. The corpus substantially exceeds the reference's node count, but over-coverage against a floor stated as "at minimum" is not a mismatch.

quality.most_important_finding: The corpus is strong, and the failure mode worth acting on is over-assertion at the edges: `ATE decomposes-into LATE`, `natural-experiment rules-out selection-bias`, and `selection-bias does-not-threaten IV-identification` each state a relationship the field does not support — the LATE is a subpopulation effect rather than a component of the ATE, and quasi-random treatment assignment does not rule out selection into the sample. These are exactly the edges a reader would take on trust because every neighboring edge is correct, so they should be downgraded to hedged relationships or removed before the graph is built on.
